I ran `crimes` against the fixture (scan, `explain` on the alias finding, `context` on the TS client) and then read the three source files to resolve what the scanner reported as `…+1 more`. **No changes made** — this is the investigation.

## The object has two names

The core domain object is the **tenant**. crimes identified this directly:

```
  4. packages/api/billing/plans.py:10
     Charge: Cross-Language Concept Alias Drift
     Summary: The "tenant" concept is called team in Python and workspace in
              TypeScript, across 3 files. An agent searching for one name finds
              only half the code it needs to change.
     Evidence:
       · Python uses: team
       · TypeScript uses: workspace
       · preferred form for this group: "organization"
```

`crimes explain` on that fingerprint spells out why it survives: *"The mapping is usually obvious to whoever wrote it and invisible to everyone since, which is why this survives long past the point where anyone remembers it was a rename that only half-happened."* That is literally what happened here — see the "already half-renamed" section below.

## Every site, both halves

crimes listed 8 and truncated with `…+1 more`; reading the files gives the full 9 plus the things a symbol-level detector doesn't report.

**Python — `team`** (`packages/api/`)
| Site | Note |
|---|---|
| `plans.py:11` | docstring "The tiers a **team** can be on" |
| `routes.py:10,15,20,25` | route paths `/api/teams`, `/api/teams/{team_id}[/seats|/plan]` |
| `routes.py:10,20,25` | `team_id` path parameter |
| `routes.py:11,16,21,26` | `get_team`, `create_team`, `team_seats`, `change_team_plan` |

**TypeScript — `workspace`** (`packages/web/`)
| Site | Note |
|---|---|
| `workspace-client.ts` | **the filename itself** — not in crimes' evidence, it reports symbols |
| lines 4–5 | module docstring, which already documents the mismatch |
| `:12` | `interface Workspace` |
| `:17,22,27,33` | `getWorkspace`, `createWorkspace`, `workspaceSeats`, `changeWorkspacePlan` (`:33` is the hidden `+1 more`) |
| `:18,23` | URLs `/api/workspaces` |

## What else you'd have to touch — four things worth stopping on

**1. `team` is overloaded — a naive find/replace corrupts the plan enum.** `plans.py:15` is `TEAM = "team"`, a *subscription tier*, not the tenant. It's also `SEATS_INCLUDED[Plan.TEAM] = 10` at `:22`. A repo-wide `team → organization` would silently change a wire value. crimes reports the alias drift and the `Plan` type drift as two independent findings; the collision *between* them is mine, and it's the single biggest trap in this rename.

**2. The rename is already half-done, and it's broken today.** The frontend uses `/api/workspaces` for two calls and `/api/teams` for the other two. The backend declares only `/api/teams*`. crimes caught one:

```
  5. Charge: Cross-Language Route Drift
     · packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:23 — POST /api/workspaces
     · 4 backend routes declared across 1 file
     · matched on literal path strings — a route or URL assembled at
       runtime is invisible to this check
```

That disclaimer matters: `getWorkspace` at `:18` builds its URL by concatenation (`"/api/workspaces/" + id`), so it is **invisible to the check but equally broken** — a second 404. So the HTTP surface is part of the rename, not a side effect of it, and picking `/api/organizations` is a breaking wire change for anything outside this repo.

**3. A method mismatch rides along on the plan route** — `PUT /api/teams/:id/plan` vs the declared `POST` (crime 3). Fails as a 405, which crimes notes "is easy to misread as a permissions problem." Worth fixing in the same pass since you're touching that path anyway.

**4. Nothing will catch a mistake.** Every finding scores `test_gap: 1.00` ("no sibling or `__tests__` test file detected") and `blast_radius: 0`. Read the blast radius carefully — it means *no other file in this repo imports these modules*, not that nothing consumes them. The Python side is a public FastAPI surface; crimes has no visibility into external callers.

## The `Plan` drift is a separate decision

crimes' highest-severity finding isn't the rename at all:

```
  1. Charge: Cross-Language Type Drift  (severity high)
     · Python declares [free, pro, team, scale]
     · TypeScript declares [free, pro, enterprise]
     · only in Python: scale, team — the TypeScript side will reject these
     · only in TypeScript: enterprise — the Python side will reject this
```

Three values disagree. It's entangled with the rename only through the `TEAM`/`team` collision, so I'd keep it a separate change — but you have to *decide* on it before renaming, because if you unify the enum you may drop `TEAM` as a tier, which changes whether the collision exists.

## Recommendation

Pick `organization` (crimes' suggested canonical, and it dodges the `team` tier collision entirely). Sequence: (a) resolve the `Plan` enum first so you know whether `TEAM` survives; (b) rename Python symbols and TS symbols by AST/symbol, never by text substitution; (c) treat the route paths as one deliberate, versioned wire change and fix the `PUT`/`POST` mismatch in the same pass; (d) rename `workspace-client.ts`; (e) add at least one contract test before any of it, since there is currently zero coverage on either side.

One low-value finding I'd skip: crime 6 (`Phantom Accomplice`) flags `enum`, `fastapi`, and `billing.plans` as undeclared — that's the Node-manifest resolver looking at Python imports; `enum` is stdlib and `billing.plans` is a local module. Not relevant to the rename.
